verses.text: But now Yahweh who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel says: “Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine.
When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they will not overflow you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned, and flame will not scorch you.
For I am Yahweh your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior. I have given Egypt as your ransom, Ethiopia and Seba in your place.
Since you have been precious and honored in my sight, and I have loved you; therefore I will give people in your place, and nations instead of your life.
Don’t be afraid; for I am with you. I will bring your offspring  from the east, and gather you from the west.
I will tell the north, ‘Give them up!’ and tell the south, ‘Don’t hold them back! Bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth —
everyone who is called by my name, and whom I have created for my glory, whom I have formed, yes, whom I have made.’”
Bring out the blind people who have eyes, and the deaf who have ears.

Let all the nations be gathered together, and let the peoples be assembled. Who among them can declare this, and show us former things? Let them bring their witnesses, that they may be justified; or let them hear, and say, “That is true.”

“You are my witnesses,” says Yahweh, “With my servant whom I have chosen; that you may know and believe me, and understand that I am he. Before me there was no God formed, neither will there be after me.
I myself am Yahweh; and besides me there is no savior.
I have declared, I have saved, and I have shown; and there was no strange god among you. Therefore you are my witnesses”, says Yahweh, “and I am God.
Yes, since the day was I am he; and there is no one who can deliver out of my hand. I will work, and who can hinder it?”
Yahweh, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel says: “For your sake, I have sent to Babylon, and I will bring all of them down as fugitives, even the Chaldeans, in the ships of their rejoicing.
I am Yahweh, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, your King.”
Yahweh, who makes a way in the sea, and a path in the mighty waters says:
who brings out the chariot and horse, the army and the mighty man (they lie down together, they shall not rise; they are extinct, they are quenched like a wick):
“Don’t remember the former things, and don’t consider the things of old.
Behold, I will do a new thing. It springs out now. Don’t you know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.
The animals of the field shall honor me, the jackals and the ostriches; because I give water in the wilderness and rivers in the desert, to give drink to my people, my chosen,
the people which I formed for myself, that they might declare my praise.
Yet you have not called on me, Jacob; but you have been weary of me, Israel.
You have not brought me of your sheep for burnt offerings; neither have you honored me with your sacrifices. I have not burdened you with offerings, nor wearied you with frankincense.
You have bought me no sweet cane with money, nor have you filled me with the fat of your sacrifices; but you have burdened me with your sins. You have wearied me with your iniquities.
I, even I, am he who blots out your transgressions for my own sake; and I will not remember your sins.
Put me in remembrance. Let us plead together. Declare your case, that you may be justified.
Your first father sinned, and your teachers have transgressed against me.
Therefore I will profane the princes of the sanctuary; and I will make Jacob a curse, and Israel an insult.”

footnotes.content: Notice how the Lord begins—not with what we must do, but with what He has already done. He created us, formed us, redeemed us, and calls us by name. Before we turn to Him, He has turned all of His power toward us. We belong to Him, fully and tenderly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The ancient Israelites knew rivers that could overflow, fires that could consume. The Lord's promise is not that hardship won't come—it will—but that He will be *with us* in it. His presence is the secret to walking unafraid through water and flame.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Ransom—Egypt, Ethiopia, Seba—given in Israel's place. This speaks to substitution, to the Lord's willingness to spend His most precious treasures on behalf of those He loves. In time, this ransom would take on flesh and blood on a hill called Golgotha.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Precious and honored in His sight—not because of what we do or produce, but because He has chosen to love us. He will give nations, peoples, even His own life in our stead. We have been weighed on His scale and found worthy of His outpouring.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From east and west He gathers His children—scattered as they are, far from home. The Lord's gathering is patient, thorough, and finds each one. He is not content until His own are brought home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The four corners of the earth listen to His word: north and south obey. What a picture of lordship—not tyranny, but the natural order when the Creator speaks and all creation hears. His sons and daughters come from the ends of the earth, answering His call.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Created for His glory, formed by His hand, made to declare His praise. We are not accidents or afterthoughts. We exist for a purpose as old as creation itself—to reflect back to Him the honor He deserves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The blind with eyes, the deaf with ears—yet still blind and deaf to the Lord's works. This speaks to a kind of hardness, a refusal to see what is plain. We can look upon His acts all our lives and still not perceive His hand if we will not.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The idols of the nations are called forth to prove themselves—to declare past things truly and be justified. But they cannot. Only the God of Israel has always known the end from the beginning. His alone is the power to make all things right.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We are witnesses—not to what we've invented, but to what we've seen Him do. To believe Him and understand who He truly is becomes our calling. The servant whom He chose stands before all nations as proof of His reality.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh Himself declares what no other can: alone He saves. There is no rival, no alternative, no backup plan. Salvation is His work and His alone, freely given to those who call on His name.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord has declared it, saved His people, and shown Himself faithful. No other god has mixed itself into this story. We stand before the nations as His witnesses, saying simply: we have seen Him work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I am he"—the great affirmation. He was before all things began, and none can stand against Him or frustrate what His hand intends. What comfort to those whose enemies seem powerful—our God cannot be hindered.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Babylon and the Chaldeans—the great power of that day, proud in their conquests—will be brought down as fugitives. The Lord sends against them and breaks their strength. He is the Redeemer who defeats even the mightiest earthly powers.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three titles in one breath: Redeemer, Holy One, King. He is set apart in His holiness, near to us in His redemption, and sovereign over all. These three truths together tell us who He is—our liberator, our holiness, our ruler.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The way in the sea—an echo of the Red Sea crossing, the founding memory of Israel's rescue. The Lord who made a path through water then is the same Lord speaking now. He has a long history of making ways where there are none.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Chariot and horse, army and mighty man—the symbols of earthly power. They lie down and do not rise; they are extinguished like a wick. No human strength endures against the Lord's will. All our pride is as a flame that flickers out.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Don't remember the former things." Not because they weren't real, but because what's coming is so much greater that looking backward will blind you to it. The Lord calls us to let go of yesterday's story and trust Him for today's new mercies.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A new thing springs forth—waters in the wilderness, rivers in the desert. The Lord is not bound by what was. He can make life flourish where logic says only death can grow. His creativity toward us knows no boundary.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even the wild animals—jackals and ostriches—honor the Lord because He has sustained them in the wasteland. What He does for His people has ripple effects through all creation. His care is not narrow but generously wide.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Formed for Himself, to declare His praise—we exist to return to Him what He has given. Our life's deepest purpose is to magnify the One who made us. Everything else—comfort, success, ease—is secondary to this.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord's complaint is not harshness but honest sorrow: you have not called on me. Instead, you have grown weary of me. It's as if He grieves that those He formed for His praise have turned away from their own purpose.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sacrificial system—burnt offerings, rams, frankincense—were meant to express devotion and dependence. But the Lord didn't burden Israel with endless ritual because what He wanted was their *hearts*, not their exhaustion. Even then, He was calling them to easier yokes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They have not brought Him honor but have instead brought their sins—making Him weary with iniquities. The Lord contrasts what should have been given with what was actually brought. We can exhaust Him not through sacrifice but through persistent rebellion.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yet here is the turn: though they have burdened Him, He Himself—He—is the one who blots out their transgressions. He doesn't remember their sins. This is grace breaking through judgment, forgiveness offered freely to those who have wearied Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Put me in remembrance"—the Lord invites us to plead our case, to argue if we can. He stands open to our questions, not threatened by them. He wants us to speak, to bring our need, that He might justify us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Your first father—Abraham—and your teachers have all sinned and transgressed. No one in Israel's long line is innocent. This is not shame but clarity: we are all bound by the same need for redemption, no matter how honored our ancestors.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord speaks of profaning the princes and making Jacob a curse. Looking back from this longer road, we see that this judgment did come—and then came restoration beyond measure. Readers today hear an echo in how the Lord breaks what must be broken in order to make us truly His.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
